questions.stem: According to Bowen Family Systems, how does change occur?

options.A: Change occurs through restructuring the family’s organization. Very focused on entire organization of the whole family system. Looking at bigger picture of the family interactions.
options.B: Change happens through self-awareness and improved communication. Humanistic approach.
options.C: Change occurs by understanding multigenerational dynamics and increasing differentiation. The only therapy that is concerned with the past three generations of the family. People’s issues are transmitted through the family.
options.D: Change occurs through action-oriented directives and paradoxical interventions. Very focused on specific problems.

According to Narrative Therapy, how does change occur?

options.A: Change occurs through accessing client’s strengths and resources. Emphasizes finding solutions to a problem, not on discovering the cause or origins of the problem.
options.B: Change happens through self-awareness and improved communication. Humanistic approach.
options.C: Views people are always growing and inherently good. Avoids diagnosis, avoid strict adherence to what the ideal person should be. Role of therapist is nondirective, not steering client in any one direction (unlike CBT or systems theory). Driven by what the client wants to talk about. T is a facilitator who is helping the person to grow and change. This occurs by creating unconditional positive regard. Client determines the goals of therapy. Up to the client to decide how many sessions they would like as well, a lot of support for client self-determination.
options.D: Change occurs by separating the person from the problem and by creating a new narrative which emphasizes the individual’s competencies and strengths.

According to Attachment-Based Therapy (Bowlby), how does change occur?

options.A: Change occurs through both reparative experiences within the treatment relationship (relationship with therapist) insight into and modification of entrenched object relations pathology.
options.B: Change occurs through empathetic attunement and strengthening the self-structures through optimal responsiveness. Shift away from interpretation.
options.C: Change occurs through exploration of past and current relational attachments and trauma in the environment of a healing, secure, and reliable relationship.
options.D: Views people are always growing and inherently good. Avoids diagnosis, avoid strict adherence to what the ideal person should be. Role of therapist is nondirective, not steering client in any one direction (unlike CBT or systems theory). Driven by what the client wants to talk about. T is a facilitator who is helping the person to grow and change. This occurs by creating unconditional positive regard. Client determines the goals of therapy. Up to the client to decide how many sessions they would like as well, a lot of support for client self-determination.

questions.stem:
Which model holds that change occurs in this way?

“Change occurs through exploration of past and current relational attachments and trauma in the environment of a healing, secure, and reliable relationship.”
According to Client Centered Therapy, how does change occur?

options.A: Views people are always growing and inherently good. Avoids diagnosis, avoid strict adherence to what the ideal person should be. Role of therapist is nondirective, not steering client in any one direction (unlike CBT or systems theory). Driven by what the client wants to talk about. T is a facilitator who is helping the person to grow and change. This occurs by creating unconditional positive regard. Client determines the goals of therapy. Up to the client to decide how many sessions they would like as well, a lot of support for client self-determination.
options.B: Change happens through the existential encounter – the authentic meeting of the therapist and the client in the present moment and by expanding the client’s range of experience. Very influenced by Gestalt therapy. Generally used with families, started by Carl Whittaker.
options.C: Change occurs through finding meaning, living authentically and responsibly. The idea that the person can respond, make choices, emphasizes personal choice about how clients want to live their lives. Core question: how do I exist? Inherent meaninglessness to life and existence.
options.D: The idea is that change occurs through increased awareness of here and now experience and dialogic relationship between T and client. Dialogic refers to a therapeutic stance where the therapist and client engage as two authentic human beings — fully present with each other, co-creating the therapeutic process. Heavily influenced by Martin Buber’s “I-Thou” philosophy, where the therapist meets the client as a fellow human, not an object to be treated.
